content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing an issue with my USB connection. On my previous laptop, everything worked fine, and I was able to transfer [product_name] programs normally. Now, with a new notebook, I’m having trouble with the interface—the program cannot detect the cable, even though the laptop itself does. I've already downloaded all the necessary drivers, but that hasn't resolved the issue. I have a deadline to present my work soon, so any help would be appreciated. Thank you, and apologies for my English.

Which operating system are you using? Is it the same version as your old computer? Make sure you've installed the [product_name] cable driver. If you’re using Windows 7, it should work well—I’ve tested it on Windows 7 Starter myself. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing challenges with USB interface detection for [product_name] when switching to a new laptop. Although the operating system recognizes the cable, the software fails to detect it, despite correct driver installation. This highlights ongoing issues with device compatibility, driver stability, and reliable software-to-hardware communication.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects a straightforward USB connection between a new laptop and the [product_name] interface, with the software successfully identifying the cable once drivers are installed.
